properties.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage (Eagle)
properties.whyLeft: The descent stage served as a stationary launch pad for the ascent stage carrying Armstrong and Aldrin back to orbit. Returning it would have required prohibitive fuel mass.
properties.scienceEnabled: Enabled humanity's first extraterrestrial touchdown, deployment of the Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR), and collection of 21.55 kg of pristine lunar rock and regolith samples.
properties.nasaSource: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) & Apollo Lunar Surface Journal
properties.funFact: The plaque on its front leg reads: 'Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon. We came in peace for all mankind.'

properties.name: Apollo 12 Descent Stage & ALSEP
properties.whyLeft: Left in place after pinpoint landing. Its passive nuclear-powered ALSEP scientific station continued transmitting seismic and solar wind data for 8 years until NASA officially powered it down in 1977.
properties.scienceEnabled: Proved precision lunar landing navigation next to Surveyor 3. Detected deep Moonquakes and measured the Moon's exceedingly weak magnetic field.
properties.funFact: Astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked over to Surveyor 3, parked just 180 meters away, making it the only time humans visited a robot on another world!

properties.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-001)
properties.whyLeft: Transporting the 210 kg electric vehicle back to orbit was impossible due to strict ascent payload weight limits. It was parked 90 meters away to broadcast the Apollo liftoff with its color TV camera.
properties.scienceEnabled: Extended exploration traverse radius to 27.9 km, allowing astronauts to climb Mount Hadley Delta and discover the famous 'Genesis Rock' (anorthosite dated to 4.1 billion years old).
properties.nasaSource: NASA Solar System Treks / Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
properties.funFact: The rover tires were made of woven zinc-coated steel wire mesh with titanium chevrons for traction instead of rubber, because rubber would crack in lunar vacuum!

properties.name: Apollo 16 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-002)
properties.whyLeft: Permanently stationed in the Descartes Highlands to record liftoff and remain as a monument to human engineering.
properties.scienceEnabled: Covered 26.7 km of terrain, disproving the prevailing theory that the Descartes Highlands were formed by ancient volcanism, proving impact cratering mechanics instead.
properties.funFact: Astronaut John Young set the lunar land-speed record in this rover, hitting an estimated 18 km/h (11.2 mph) downhill!

properties.name: Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-003)
properties.whyLeft: The final manned rover left on the Moon. Parked at 'VIP Site' 150 meters east of the Challenger descent stage so its ground-controlled RCA television camera could capture human departure.
properties.scienceEnabled: Traversed 35.9 km across the deep Taurus-Littrow valley. Allowed geologist Harrison Schmitt to discover orange volcanic glass soil beads formed 3.64 billion years ago.
properties.funFact: When an astronaut accidentally knocked off the right rear fender, they repaired it with lunar maps, duct tape, and clamps!

properties.name: Surveyor 1 Lunar Soft Lander
properties.whyLeft: Pre-Apollo unmanned robotic precursor. Completed mission when extreme -150°C lunar night drained its onboard batteries.
properties.scienceEnabled: Transmitted 11,237 television photos and proved that lunar soil had adequate bearing strength to support a manned Apollo spacecraft without sinking into quicksand.
properties.funFact: Before Surveyor 1 landed, some scientists feared the Moon was covered in miles of soft dust that would swallow spaceships whole!

properties.name: Surveyor 3 Lunar Lander
properties.whyLeft: Stationary lander in Ocean of Storms. Apollo 12 astronauts visited it 2.5 years later and dismantled parts to study deep space exposure.
properties.scienceEnabled: Dug trenches into lunar soil with a robotic scoop and proved soil mechanics. Returned parts provided the first real baseline on cosmic radiation wear on human electronics.
properties.funFact: When Apollo 12 returned Surveyor 3's camera to Earth, scientists detected Streptococcus mitis bacteria inside, sparking a debate on whether life survived 2.5 years on the Moon!

properties.name: LCROSS Shepherding Spacecraft & Centaur Stage
properties.mission: Lunar CRater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS)
properties.whyLeft: Deliberately guided into a permanently shadowed lunar crater at 9,000 km/h to excavate subterranean volatile materials into sunlight for spectroscopic analysis.
properties.scienceEnabled: Confirmed the presence of water ice inside permanently shadowed craters at the lunar south pole, calculating roughly 5.6% water mass in the plume.
properties.funFact: The impact created a crater 20 meters wide and kicked up an estimated 350 metric tons of lunar debris!

properties.name: Lunar Prospector Orbiter
properties.whyLeft: Intentionally crashed into Shoemaker Crater at the Moon's South Pole at mission end to search for water vapor plumes.
properties.scienceEnabled: Mapped lunar gravity, magnetic field, and created the first complete global neutron spectrometer map proving elevated hydrogen concentrations at the poles.
properties.funFact: Carried a tiny capsule of the cremated ashes of famed planetary geologist Eugene Shoemaker, making him the only human buried on the Moon.
